content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question: Is it possible to connect an analog input (0-10V) so that it influences the delay time of a function block? For example: At 0V, the on-delay is 20ms At 5V, the on-delay is 40ms At 10V, the on-delay is 60ms These are just example values, not final timings. Does anyone know if this type of setup is achievable? Thanks in advance [user_name]

Hi, I think this should be achievable, though not in the most straightforward manner. My suggestion: 1. Use analog threshold triggers for your analog input. 2. Set up a threshold trigger for each delay time you need, using appropriate voltage levels for configuration. 3. Connect these triggers to timers (make sure the triggers are interlocked). You can then use the timers to change the function timing as required. Others may have an alternative or simpler method. [user_name]

Thank you for the quick response, [user_name]. That approach sounds reasonable, but I’d need at least five triggers to cover all the timing options I want. I was hoping to directly link the analog input to a timing parameter inside a function block, but looks like that’s a bit complicated. Back to the drawing board for now. Appreciate your help! [user_name]

Hello! If you use basic time blocks, it’s possible to use an analog input as a reference for the timers. However, you’ll need the latest [product_name] (with ordering numbers ending in [article_no]) and the newest [product_name] software [version_no]. I created a small sample—see the attachment.
